pr_title: [ML] shore up the ML feature reset code and fix potential bugs
pr_body:
The ML feature reset code was originally force closing all datafeeds, anomaly jobs, and analytics jobs.

This does not allow the caller to wait for the persistent tasks to complete. It is possible for a persistent task
to NOT exist in cluster state, but the individual node task is still executing. But, there is no visibility.

To prevent this from causing issues and more complexity in the feature reset code, this commit
attempts to close/stop all datafeeds, jobs, and data frame jobs without force first. If that fails, then
force is attempted.

additionally, this commit addresses two gaps in the reset mode handling:

- In the bulk execution retry, this was previously ignoring the reset mode flag
- In trained model stats persister, this was also ignoring the reset mode flag

closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/71282

issue_context.title: TestFeatureResetIT#testMLFeatureReset due to IndexNotFoundException and index existance
issue_context.body:

Either way, ML seems to be creating an index right when (or immediately after) the feature cleanup is called.

review_comments:
I think there is a nasty edge case with this.

The scenario is that a reset starts and finishes while this class is sleeping between retries.  Then when it wakes up it writes documents that were retrying from before the refresh.

One way around this that I can think of is to have an incrementing count of how many times reset mode has toggled.  Any scheduled retries that wake up check if that count is different to what it was when they were originally scheduled, and if there's a difference they do nothing.

Another way might be to cancel any scheduled retries when this reset mode flag changes value.

> Another way might be to cancel any scheduled retries when this reset mode flag changes value.

This might be the easiest way as we already keep track of which retryable actions are inflight. Will just have to separate out the search and the bulk inflight actions.
